question: Which Governor General of India Proposed the Vernacular press act in 1878?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Vernacular Press Act, 1878, was introduced by Viceroy Lord Lytton during his tenure (1876–1880).
 
• The act aimed to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press, which was critical of British policies, particularly during events like the Great Famine of 1876–78.
 
• The act symbolized British efforts to control dissent and curb nationalist sentiments in India.
 
• It was repealed in 1882 by Lord Ripon, the succeeding Viceroy, as part of his liberal policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **​Lord Hardinge**
 
 
• Lord Hardinge__ served as Viceroy of India from 1910 to 1916.
 
• Lord Hardinge was the Viceroy when the Royal Commission on Civil Services was formed in 1912.
 __
 
• The Royal Commission on Public Services in India is also known as the Islington Commission.
 
• It was created under the Chairmanship of Lord Islington.
 
 
 
• He shifted India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.
 
• Bengal partition was cancelled by Lord Hardinge in 1911.
 
• 'Defence of India Act' was passed by Lord Hardinge in 1915.
 
• George V and Queen Mary visited India during the period of Lord Hardinge.
 
 

 
• Lord Minto:__

 
 
• Gilbert Elliot-Murray-Kynynmound, 1st Earl of Minto, served as the Governor-General of India from 1807 to 1813.
 
• He focused on improving relations with the Indian princely states and played a key role in the Anglo-Maratha Wars.
